questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was important for me to go on exchange to a place where I could feel at home, while still experiencing a different culture, without being too far away from home. I therefore felt that Italy was the perfect destination, as I have always felt a strong affection for the country, while at the same time it is not very far from Denmark.
I believe that what particularly attracted me to Milan was the strong Danish community there. Although I find other Italian cities more attractive in some respects, it meant a great deal to me that many other Danish students were also going on exchange, especially since I was travelling alone. In addition, Milan is very centrally located, making it easy to travel around Italy. This was also a decisive factor in my choice of Milan, as it opened up many opportunities for travelling throughout the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I found it really confusing in the beginning, especially because the course selection process was very unclear and, in practice, something that was only resolved once the classes had already started. I found this particularly frustrating.
Otherwise, the process was manageable, as it was easy to contact staff members in Milan, and we also had an information meeting at home, which helped ensure that we were reasonably well informed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received several emails informing us that we had to report our arrival at the Erasmus office, and we also received emails regarding course selection. However, I feel that the information could have been communicated more clearly and in a more informative way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found my apartment through Airbnb. It is a slightly more expensive way of finding accommodation, but I felt that it offered a greater sense of security. I would therefore recommend booking accommodation early (if using Airbnb), as in most cases you can book well in advance and cancel close to the start date if you find something better.
I booked my apartment as early as January, even though I was not leaving until September, and I would definitely recommend doing the same.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I did not actually meet anyone who lived on campus. Everyone I met lived in their own apartments, and it seemed to work perfectly fine for them.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The entire process of registering for courses was very confusing. There was very little information provided until just around the time of arrival. In addition, putting together a course schedule was extremely difficult, at least in my case, and it varied greatly from student to student. I had received pre-approval for around 15 courses, and there was not a single combination of these courses that did not involve timetable clashes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to communicate with some members of the university staff.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
As mentioned earlier, it was not really possible for me to put together a schedule without my courses overlapping. This was therefore very frustrating, as I had to figure out which courses I could take without being required to attend every session. Fortunately, this was possible for most courses, as there were options such as being registered as non-attending, or where attendance was not mandatory.
In addition, it was possible during the first two weeks to try out different courses, which also made the process a bit easier. As a result, I did not have my final schedule until around the end of September.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to get as many courses pre-approved as possible, as it is reassuring not to have to apply for pre-approval while you are already abroad, but instead be able to choose freely among the courses you have already had approved.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I would say that the overall academic level is somewhat lower than at my home university. I took three master’s level courses and one bachelor’s level course, and I did not feel that the master’s courses were noticeably more advanced than my own academic level.
That being said, it could at times be extremely difficult to understand what the lecturers were saying. Several of my lecturers had very strong Italian accents, and it was often almost impossible to understand them, which naturally made the classes more challenging.
In addition, in one of my courses we were required to give a presentation where the lecturer expected us to demonstrate knowledge from our bachelor’s degree, as he assumed that we already held a bachelor’s degree in the subject of the course. This was somewhat challenging, as we were all actually completely new to the subject.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was actually very similar, as we primarily have a lot of classroom-based teaching in rhetoric, which was also the main form of teaching in Milan. Courses often included both presentations and written assignments, which contributed to the final grade, and I actually found this quite beneficial. In addition, the exams were very different from those in Denmark. The written exams were handwritten and not very well organised. The oral exam I attended also took place in front of the entire class, which I found somewhat uncomfortable.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Corporate communication 
Journalism, media and politics 
Media theory and AI 
Introduction to italian literature

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Journalism, Media and Politics. I was especially impressed by Christopher Anderson, who is an American lecturer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really participate in activities organised by the university. I attended one welcome event, but otherwise I did not take part in many university-organised activities. I mainly participated in events planned by ESN and International week.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were quite a few opportunities to join sports clubs, but it was not really something I engaged in. In addition, a number of parties were organised, but this was also not something many of us Danes participated in. We mostly spent time together with other Danish students and found our own activities to take part in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend participating in some of the parties, especially at the beginning. Otherwise, I would say that it might be better to try to find your own activities and experiences.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend travelling around Italy. Milan is a great city with excellent transport connections throughout the country, so I would recommend this one hundred percent.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine, and I did not find it particularly difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food :)))

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make the most of your time and explore as much of the country as possible.
2. Dare to do things on your own, even if it feels uncomfortable at first.
3. Remember that everyday life will eventually set in, so try not to overwhelm yourself. It is also completely okay to take time for yourself, even though it can be easy to feel like you are missing out if you are not part of everything.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient with the Italian education system, as it is very different from the Danish one. They have a very laissez-faire approach to education. In addition, the examination formats are also quite different: written exams are handwritten, and oral exams often take place in front of the entire class.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely the opportunity to travel extensively around the country. In addition, I made many great Danish friends, but I also learned a lot about myself, as I went abroad on my own and lived alone for the first time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely having to live alone and manage on your own in a completely new country. It can be intimidating at first, but I believe it makes you much more independent and teaches you a great deal.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
